title: Opinie
note:
Opinion/discussion register named on B1-SPINE.md's own line: moim zdaniem, zgadzać się, mieć rację, na pewno, może — all confirmed via check_new.py before writing. Added nie zgadzać się as the natural negative pairing (na szczęście/niestety precedent from b1_stories), matching the spine's own habit of logging a small addition rather than stretching a five-item list artificially.

ZERO NEW STRUCTURES. zgadzać się is a plain present_am reflexive verb (learner already owns the full present_am rule and sie_reflexive from a2_routine); mieć rację is mieć + Accusative, the same miec_acc job already known from mam kawę. Every sentence recycles a structure already live — deliberately spread wide rather than leaning on the last grammar unit only, per SEQUENCING.md's own recycle guidance: superlative, adverb_comp (b1_adverb_comp, the unit immediately before this one), inst_z, perf_future, motion_prefixed, conditional_sg, virile_reco/virile_nom, vocative_chunk (b1_vocative_chunks, also immediately before this one) all appear at least once.

SCOPE CUT, logged: the spine's own register also invites 'I'm wrong' as the natural opposite of mieć rację. Real Polish is nie mieć racji — GENITIVE after the negated mieć, the already-owned nie mam X + Gen pattern (a1_negation) — but racja's genitive is racji, a soft -cja-noun genitive ending this course has never taught or generalised (a1_gen_ki's k/g-stem -i exception is a different consonant class). Stacking a new genitive sub-pattern onto a vocab-only leaf was judged the wrong load; used nie zgadzać się for the negative-opinion register instead, which needs zero new grammar. If James wants nie mieć racji later, it is not on the current B1-SPINE as its own slot.

HOMOGRAPH, flagged LOUDLY, same treatment as b1_dative_pron's ci/ci and b1_ktory_cases' ktorej/ktorej: może is already taught by trunk_can_a1 as the 3sg present of moc — 'he/she/it CAN' (on moze = he can). This unit re-teaches the identical string as a completely different, unrelated word: the sentence adverb 'maybe / perhaps'. check_new.py moze correctly reports TAUGHT, citing trunk_can_a1 — that is NOT license to skip re-teaching; the two senses are disambiguated explicitly in this pack's own intro-equivalent (the item's explain string) and kept apart by context in every sentence, never by a meta quiz question. moze the adverb is re-listed in teaches_lemmas for exactly the reason ci was in b1_dative_pron: same string, genuinely new function, logged rather than assumed free.

A SECOND, LIGHTER instance of the same treatment: zdanie was already taught by leaf_school_a1 as 'sentence' (a grammar-class noun). moim zdaniem uses the same word in Polish's other everyday sense, 'opinion/view' (literally close to 'by my judgement') — a real polysemy, not an unrelated homograph like moze/moze, but still named explicitly in the item's explain string so the two senses don't blur for a learner who has only ever met zdanie in a classroom context.

BONUS PAYOFF, not a new teach: mysle is already taught (a2_o_loc, 'I think [about]') and bare ze is already taught (b1_polite, tagged as its own standalone teaches_lemma, not only inside the frozen Przepraszam-that-I'm-disturbing chunk). Combining them as Mysle, ze... ('I think that...') is therefore zero new vocabulary and zero new structure — both pieces already sit in the pool as independently reusable lemmas — but it is the single most useful sentence an opinions unit can hand over, so one example was built on it and logged here rather than silently assumed safe.

items.explain: zdanie already means sentence from school (leaf_school_a1). Here the same word is used in its other everyday sense — opinion, view — literally closer to 'by my judgement.' Same word, a genuinely different everyday meaning.

HOMOGRAPH: this is a different może from on może (he can/may) — that może is a verb form of móc; this może is an unrelated adverb meaning maybe. Same spelling, two separate words — watch the sentence around it.

sentences.en: In my opinion, this book is the best.
sentences.pl: Moim zdaniem, ta książka jest najlepsza.
accepts: Moim zdaniem, ta książka jest najlepsza.
Moim zdaniem, ta książka jest najlepsza

sentences.en: In my opinion, he speaks the fastest.
sentences.explain: najszybciej never changes shape — the same invariant adverb from b1_adverb_comp, now doing real work in an opinion.

sentences.en: I think that you are right.
sentences.explain: Myślę and że are both already yours (a2_o_loc, b1_polite) — this is the first time they combine into I think that…, the real payoff of owning both separately.
This może opens the sentence and means maybe — a different word from on może (he can), even though the spelling is identical.

sentences.en: I would like to ask whether you agree.

sentences.pl: Ci studenci na pewno mają rację.
accepts: Ci studenci na pewno mają rację.
Ci studenci na pewno mają rację

sentences.en: Mom, in my opinion that's a great present.
sentences.pl: Mamo, moim zdaniem to świetny prezent.
accepts: Mamo, moim zdaniem to świetny prezent.
Mamo, moim zdaniem to świetny prezent
